subject: MSA & Order Form — downstream vendor transition: encryption clause proposal + DPA evidence checklist
messages:
From: Natalie Gomez <natalie.gomez@datasync.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Paul Chen <paul.chen@datasync.io>
Date: 2028-05-01T08:15:00-04:00
Subject: Downstream vendor assignment — notice + DPA exhibit

Hi Hannah,

Quick heads-up from our side: we're planning to move the managed telemetry ingestion pipeline for the EU region from Vendor A to Vendor B (Datasync is the customer; Vendor B is a subcontractor engaged by Datasync). This will impact the MSA/Order Form flow-down: Datasync wants Vendor B to be listed as an approved subcontractor and to accept the DPA Exhibit A controls.

Attached: Datasync_subproc_change_notice.pdf and Datasync_DPA_Exhibit_A.pdf (exhibit contains targeted EU data handling clauses and encryption-at-rest language).

Key asks from Datasync:
- Confirmation that Redwood will accept the limited downstream delegation to Vendor B (Vendor B will only process pseudonymized telemetry)
- Acceptance of Exhibit A (Datasync requests vendor signature on the Annex) or an explicit redline if we cannot accept a clause
- Evidence of SOC2 + encryption at rest (Datasync team will need the evidence pack to route to their procurement and privacy teams)

Can you confirm the internal review path and an expected timeline? They are targeting a May 12th go-live for the migration.

Thanks,
Natalie
--
Natalie Gomez
Senior Procurement Manager, Datasync Analytics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Natalie Gomez <natalie.gomez@datasync.io>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-01T09:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Downstream vendor assignment — notice + DPA exhibit

Hi Natalie — thanks for the notice and the attachments. Looping in Legal (Markus), Procurement (Laura) and our Security/Privacy lead (Karthik) to triage.

Immediate responses:
- We will not sign a blanket subprocessor delegation without reviewing the exact scope and controls.
- If Vendor B will only process pseudonymized telemetry, that narrows the risk surface — please confirm the exact data elements and whether any user identifiers will be present.
- We'll pull SOC 2 evidence and prepare a short evidence bundle (cert + recent bridge letter + encryption config summary).

Markus / Karthik / Laura — could you:
1) Review Exhibit A and flag any non-starters (encryption language, data localization, audit rights, and retention)
2) Confirm whether we can accept a signature on the Exhibit or whether we need a redlined Annex + Order Form amendment
3) Tell Natalie a target date we can commit to for providing evidence to Datasync procurement (they want to gate go-live by May 12)

I'll coordinate the internal sign-off path.

Hannah
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-02T10:18:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Downstream vendor assignment — notice + DPA exhibit

Thanks Hannah — reviewed Exhibit A. High-level legal notes (summary for procurement & security):

1) Encryption clause: Exhibit requires AES-256 at rest and TLS1.3 in transit — we can confirm TLS1.3 and AES-256 support on the service but need to annotate that the enforcement is at the infra/config level (we cannot guarantee third-party managed instances beyond our managed fleet). Suggest redline: replace absolute warranty language with a representation of current config + commitment to maintain industry standard encryption and provide config snapshot on request.

2) Audit and subcontractor flow-down: Exhibit asks for unlimited audit rights over Vendor B. We should:
   - Accept a targeted audit window tied to specific incidents or yearly compliance attestations.
   - Add requirement that Vendor B will provide SOC2 Type II report and an attestation to the same DPA controls.

3) Retention & deletion: Need clarity on the retention trigger (who instructs deletion — Redwood or Datasync) and proof of deletion. Ask for a narrow process-driven deletion requirement (e.g., within 30 days of contract termination / customer instruction) plus certification from Vendor B.

4) Data localization: Exhibit includes a hard EU-only residency requirement. If Vendor B is EU-hosted, OK; but if they replicate outside EU for redundancy, we must accept contractual carve-outs or propose an approved list of regions.

Next steps:
- Karthik: can you confirm whether the proposed encryption redline is acceptable from Security (we need the exact wording we can share).
- Laura: procurement — can you confirm if Datasync will accept the SOC2 + attestation in lieu of an unlimited audit? Also, can you ask Datasync for exact list of data elements so we can confirm pseudonymization?

If Datasync insists on the current Exhibit without amendment, we will need a legal-level exception and an exec approval because it imposes open-ended audit obligations.

-Markus
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Natalie Gomez <natalie.gomez@datasync.io>
Date: 2028-05-03T14:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Downstream vendor assignment — notice + DPA exhibit

Short procurement update for the thread:

- I've asked Datasync for the data element list and to confirm Vendor B's hosting regions. I also requested that they accept a SOC 2 + vendor attestation instead of a wide audit clause; they said they'd escalate but no firm answer yet.
- I've uploaded a drafted "Order Form amendment" that links Vendor B as an approved subcontractor and references Exhibit A with our proposed redlines. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDPA-checklist
- DocuSign path: Datasync prefers their envelope (they shared a link). If legal signs our redline, we can route via DocuSign and aim to have signatures within 48 hours.

Timeline ask: if Security + Legal provide sign-off language by EOD May 4, I can get procurement counter-signed and completed before May 11 (tight but possible).

Laura
Sr. Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Markus / Karthik — can you both confirm the final sign-off wording for the encryption and audit items? I drafted the compliance checklist (attached as a short summary) and plan to send the redline to Datasync by tomorrow morning unless there are objections.

If we need an exception, call that out now — I will escalate to Emily (CRO) for approval.

Natalie / Paul — thanks for the prompt notice. We'll aim to provide the SOC2 evidence bundle + our redlined Exhibit A by 2028-05-05 10:00 AM ET. If anything changes on our side that impacts the timeline I will update this thread immediately.

Attachments: compiled_evidence_bundle_summary.txt (summary of SOC2 cert, bridge letter, encryption config snapshot)

Hannah
